FR-001.title: The application MUST issue an interactive system notification whenever a new player command becomes the current pending approval request.

FR-002.title: Notification coverage MUST include every existing player command approval mode, including terminal navigation commands that use the separate navigation approval state.

FR-003.title: Each notification MUST identify the requested command and present the confirmation message already used by the in-app approval prompt.

FR-004.title: Each notification MUST expose no private session or player data beyond the command information already available in the in-app approval prompt.

FR-005.title: Each interactive approval notification MUST offer actions to approve and reject the request.

FR-006.title: A notification action MUST resolve the exact request represented by that notification through the same authoritative validation and decision rules as the corresponding in-app action.

FR-007.title: Only the current pending request MUST be eligible for a notification decision; stale, repeated, malformed, or mismatched responses MUST NOT affect another request or repeat a command effect.

FR-008.title: The application MUST emit at most one newly delivered notification for each unique pending request, including across repeated state updates.

FR-009.title: The existing in-app approval prompt MUST remain available and synchronized with decisions made from system notifications.

FR-010.title: Resolution through either surface MUST prevent a second effective decision for the same request.

FR-011.title: A resolved request's notification MUST become non-actionable and MUST be removed or updated where the operating system permits.

FR-012.title: The application MUST follow the operating system's notification authorization process, respect denial or revocation, and avoid repeated unsolicited permission prompts.

FR-013.title: Notification denial, unsupported notification behavior, delivery failure, or response failure MUST NOT cancel, approve, reject, or otherwise alter the pending command by itself.

FR-014.title: When a notification action fails, the application MUST avoid reporting a successful decision and MUST preserve the existing in-app path to the authoritative request state.

FR-015.title: Notification responses MUST remain confined to the trusted Overseer application boundary and MUST NOT add any player-facing or remote approval capability.

FR-016.title: After broadcast end, terminal switch, request replacement, or application shutdown invalidates a request, any later response from its notification MUST be rejected as stale.

approach: Observe accepted authoritative coordination states in a nonblocking root adapter, present one best-effort native notification per pending request, and route validated actions through the existing App decision methods. Keep notification lifecycle failures isolated so the unchanged in-app approval path always remains authoritative and usable.

decisions.decision: Wrap the pinned Wails notification service in a nonfatal root lifecycle adapter.
decisions.why: Direct service startup can fail on unavailable native notification environments and must not abort the application.
decisions.rejected: Register the Wails notification service directly or add another notification dependency.

decisions.decision: Observe accepted App coordination publication and reuse existing App decision methods.
decisions.why: This keeps notifications synchronized with the in-app prompt and preserves server-authoritative validation, persistence, and events.
decisions.rejected: Watch frontend events, call control directly, or move notification behavior into domain packages.

decisions.decision: Correlate callbacks with one private in-memory current-request record.
decisions.why: Old, delayed, malformed, repeated, and replacement-request callbacks must be inert before they reach App validation.
decisions.rejected: Trust callback UserInfo or persist handled notification IDs.

decisions.decision: Check and request notification authorization once per launch outside application locks.
decisions.why: The Overseer window and in-app approval path must not wait on user consent, and denial must not cause prompt loops.
decisions.rejected: Block Wails startup or request permission for every command.

decisions.decision: Treat native notification removal as advisory and stale validation as mandatory.
decisions.why: The pinned Windows backend cannot remove delivered toasts, so correctness cannot depend on visual cleanup.
decisions.rejected: Assume removal or update-by-ID works consistently on every platform.

decisions.decision: Use deterministic fake-driven race coverage as completion evidence and matching-host native journeys as supplemental checks.
decisions.why: System notification centers and authorization prompts are not deterministic CI resources, while the constitution requires unavailable native checks to be reported honestly.
decisions.rejected: Gate feature completion on live notification tests for every target or omit native smoke guidance.

decisions.decision: Observe accepted coordination snapshots through one unexported App dependency after frontend event publication.
decisions.why: This preserves current event ordering and keeps notification behavior out of the frontend binding surface.
decisions.rejected: Polling App state or registering the native Wails service directly.

decisions.decision: Wrap the pinned Wails notification service in an application-owned best-effort lifecycle with asynchronous authorization.
decisions.why: Native startup or consent failures must never abort Wails startup or block the in-app approval path.
decisions.rejected: Returning native lifecycle errors to Wails or waiting for consent during startup/shutdown.

decisions.decision: Correlate callbacks only with the in-memory current record and route decisions through existing App methods.
decisions.why: The existing App/control locks remain the sole authority and stale or attacker-controlled callback metadata cannot select a request.
decisions.rejected: Parsing notification IDs or trusting callback UserInfo.

decisions.decision: Embed a cryptographically random per-launch correlation value in each native notification ID
decisions.why: The callback exposes the notification ID reliably, and matching it rejects an old-process toast even when the restored request reuses its kind and server request ID
decisions.rejected: Trust callback UserInfo or correlate only by kind and request ID

decisions.decision: Revalidate generation and stopped state after acquiring nativeMu, with an explicit shutdown-cleanup allowance
decisions.why: Queued send and remove work then becomes inert across shutdown while the shutdown-owned removal remains serialized before native ServiceShutdown
decisions.rejected: Wait synchronously for all native work during ServiceShutdown

decisions.decision: Recheck authorization once after a notification send failure and disable delivery when denial or an authorization error is observed
decisions.why: This detects runtime revocation without reopening consent or affecting the authoritative in-app request
decisions.rejected: Infer revocation from error text or retry permission and delivery on every later request

plan.summary: Planned a nonfatal root notification adapter that mirrors authoritative approval state and safely reuses existing decisions.
plan.key_finding: The native Wails service must be wrapped because direct startup failure would otherwise abort the application, and Windows cleanup cannot be the safety boundary.
